title: Ag-Embedded Laser-Induced Graphene as a Catalyst for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction in Alkaline Media
content: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a critical process in fuel cells, yet its slow kinetics necessitates efficient and cost-effective catalysts. Anion exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs) offer a promising platform for ORR electrocatalysis, as the alkaline environment enables the use of non-precious metals and carbonaceous materials. Herein, we utilize a simple, solid-state, reagent-free, and one-step synthesis of silver nanoparticle-decorated laser-induced graphene (Ag@LIG) via direct CO$\mathrm{_2}$ laser writing on a polyimide film coated with an edible silver leaf. The laser treatment simultaneously converts the polymer into a porous three-dimensional graphene network and incorporates metallic silver nanoparticles ($\sim$5--50 nm) into the carbon matrix. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the metallic nature of the incorporated silver and a marked increase in nitrogen content from ~2 at.% in pristine LIG to ~11 at.% in Ag@LIG, with pyrrolic nitrogen as the dominant configuration. Electrochemical characterization demonstrates that Ag@LIG exhibits significantly enhanced ORR activity compared to pristine LIG, with a $\sim$50 mV positive shift in onset potential and a predominantly four-electron pathway over the entire potential range, indicating efficient reduction of O$\mathrm{_2}$ to OH- with minimal peroxide (HO$\mathrm{_2^-}$) formation. The enhanced performance likely arises from the interplay between metallic silver nanoparticles and the nitrogen-doped carbon support, where the nitrogen-rich carbon matrix provides favorable O$\mathrm{_2}$ adsorption sites and the embedded Ag nanoparticles promote O--O bond cleavage. This work highlights the potential of the solid-state laser approach for producing Ag-carbon hybrid electrocatalysts with promising ORR performance for alkaline fuel cells.
